## Raycast support
CueNow now works with [Raycast](https://raycast.com). Five commands, each of which you can give its own hotkey:
- **Create Note** — opens a new sticky note, focused and ready to type in - **Search Notes** — find any note by its title *or* by something written inside it, then open, hide, copy or delete it - **Show All Notes** — brings every note back onto the screen - **Hide All Notes** — clears every note off the screen without deleting anything - **Open Settings** — opens the settings window
The extension is pending review on the Raycast Store.
## Control CueNow from anywhere
CueNow now answers `cuenow://` links, so Shortcuts, scripts, or anything that can open a URL can drive it:
``` cuenow://new-note cuenow://show-all-notes cuenow://hide-all-notes cuenow://settings ```
Commands always go to the copy of CueNow you already have running rather than starting a second one.
## Fixed
- Opening Settings from a link no longer does nothing when CueNow wasn't already running.

# CueNow 1.5.0
macOS 27 compatibility release.
- Fixed notes that could not be dragged on macOS 27. Dragging now goes through AppKit, so dragging a note to a screen edge tiles it again. - Note transparency now follows the system. Glass notes pick up the Liquid Glass transparency setting in System Settings → Appearance instead of staying at a fixed opacity. - Glass notes and the menu bar menu now turn opaque when Reduce Transparency is on. - Rebuilt the menu bar menu as a real menu surface: system glass, the correct corner radius, and the standard gap below the menu bar, replacing the popover arrow and chrome it used before. - Fixed a hard rectangular edge drawn around the menu bar menu's rounded corners. - Fixed the blur behind the menu bar menu keeping square corners on macOS 13–15. - Adopted the macOS 27 status item API so the menu keeps correct keyboard focus and menu bar tracking.
Requires macOS 13 or later.

# CueNow 1.4.6
- Fixed `1.Text` on older macOS rendering with a mismatched number font or an unintended list-style gap. - Preserved normal numbered-list formatting for `1. Text`.
